correctness.rationale: Take an X-letter x0 and rotate between its occurrences: each Y-letter must appear once in each interval by cross-part alternation; every other X-letter must occur twice together in one interval, enclosing that interval’s Y-occurrences, and nested X-intervals give P B P^R; the opposite interval similarly Q C Q^R. Y nonalternation forces C=B^R; rotation produces A B A^R B^R. Reverse construction verifies alternation for every cross edge and nonalternation within each part. Parameter pairs (A,B) and (A^R,B^R) give the sole cyclic duplication when N=m+n>=3, with 2N distinct rotations; count follows. Graph is connected and not complete for N>=3, so published square-free theorem applies. Independently enumerated all 2N-letter double-occurrence words through N=5 (113400 at N=5), for every bipartition, and matched the classification and counts. Infinite all-m,n proof is the nesting argument.
residual_risks: Cycles count identifies rotations but not reversal as a separate equivalence.
N=2 has a special periodicity and representation-number exception, handled separately.

value.rationale: This classifies an entire representation-number-minimal word layer for the fundamental connected noncomplete family K_mn and counts labeled linear and cyclic words. The exact classification is a natural answer to the original source’s word-counting direction and a usable reference for double-occurrence word enumeration, not an arbitrary small parameter slice.
residual_risks: Specific to bipartite complete graphs and 2-uniform layer; does not count all higher-uniformity squarefree words.

final_claim: Every 2-uniform representing word of labeled complete bipartite K_{m,n}, m,n>=1, is a cyclic rotation of A B A^R B^R with A,B permutations of the fixed parts. The linear count is (m+n)m!n!; if m+n>=3 the cyclic count is m!n!/2 and all such words are square-free. For K1,1 the two linear words abab,baba are square words and cyclically equivalent.
limitations: Parts fixed and labeled; cyclic equivalence rotates but does not quotient by all relabelings.
Exceptional K1,1 separately non-squarefree and representation number 1.
Finite brute force through N=5 is not used to prove generality.
